fields.reasoning: Runs 01M7GG7GXSA97HESRNFEBFCZ4T and 01M7GG7HSBSB356BVGGQGH8YHB went check -> gate right after the arbiter wrote its Decision (internal/workflow/builtin/plan.toml), so the accepted plan still carried the confirmed major and a builder later applied the ruling by hand. The arbiter guide forbids the arbiter writing anything but its Decision, so applying it is the reviser's job, as revising is for rounds 1 and 2. The intent offers the run failing instead of accepting as the alternative; failing after one apply visit gives both. A re-review is not added: review is capped at 3 visits and the rulings check is mechanical.
fields.statement: In an autonomous plan run, a confirmed major left after review round 3 is decided by the arbiter and then applied to the plan before the gate: the check step passes to a rulings step (rhiza run review-check --rulings), which fails while a passed ruling is unapplied and sends the run to one apply-rulings visit of the plan reviser; a ruling still unapplied after it ends the run failed before the gate, so the gate never accepts a plan whose confirmed major the arbiter ruled on but nobody applied. An arbiter that cannot decide still fails the run naming the question. A normal run, whose review questions stay open for the owner, is unchanged.

fields.reasoning: The model has no other mechanical sign that a node followed a Decision; decided-by is the link every leaf uses for its Decisions and modellint.UnappliedDecisions already reads it the same way. Field-diff checks would need to guess which field the ruling changes. The finding's node can be a Decision in a landed record (plan-workflow-autonomous-left.txtar's keep-flat), so the check accepts any live node kind, written in any change set.
fields.statement: A ruling counts as applied when a live node links decided-by to the arbiter's Decision. The arbiter writes only the answers link to the question, so the reviser who changes the finding's node per the ruling links that node decided-by the Decision; the link is what rhiza run review-check --rulings tests. Only rulings whose arbitration passed count; open questions (a normal run) and failed arbitrations (which already fail the run) are not looked at.

fields.reasoning: internal/api/run.go sets Answered only when the engine delivers to an asking session (an answered entry), which never happens for a session-less ask (engine.go arbitrateAsked: 'No session asked, so nothing is delivered'), so every review ruling reads 'not yet delivered', the symptom the intent quotes.
fields.statement: Run status says 'not yet delivered' only for a question a session asked and is waiting on. A question no session asked (a review question journalled by rhiza run review-check) has nothing to deliver: its passed ruling prints as '— decision <handle>' alone. RunQuestion gains an omitempty session field (the asking session) so the markdown can tell them apart; the --json change is additive.

Failure case: a passed ruling whose Decision has only its answers link fails with an error naming the question handle and the Decision handle, and the same with the only decided-by link retired.
fields.must_not: Change what review-check does without --rulings, its conductor path (checksDeclaringStep) or the questions it adds at round 3; write to the model or the journal; count a question a session asked.
fields.statement: rhiza run review-check --rulings passes when every review question of the run (a session-less asked entry) whose arbitration passed has its answering Decision applied, a live node linking decided-by to it, and when there is no such question; otherwise it exits non-zero listing each unapplied ruling (question handle, Decision handle, the node of the finding it came from) with next rhiza run status. It judges and writes nothing.

fields.statement: The built-in plan and plan-milestone workflows pass check to a rulings command step (run = rhiza run review-check --rulings, max_visits 2, on.pass gate, on.fail apply-rulings) and add an apply-rulings agent step (prompt '/rhiza-plan-reviser Apply the arbiter's rulings on the plan of change set {change}: follow rhiza guide plan-reviser.', until true, until_when done, max_visits 1, on.pass rulings), so a ruling still unapplied after one apply visit ends the run failed before the gate.

fields.failure_waiver: Guide text only: the test asserts the text is present; there is no runtime failure path in this leaf (the run failing on an unapplied ruling is plan-workflow-applies-rulings' failure case).
